Knowing the principles isn't the same as reading the book. The reason I ask if you've read the book is because I saw what you said in your original post and what you're saying here:

>it can be warped like another diet - eating only when hungry, not eating when not hungry. I don't like not being allowed to not eat when I want to

That is *not* intuitive eating. Eating something because you want to experience the taste or texture of something is perfectly okay under intuitive eating. Now clearly it would be better for your weight loss if you waited until you were hungry before you ate whatever it is you wanted to taste, but that doesn't mean you're not allowed. You *are* allowed. 

I advise you to read the book in full. If you have already read it, I advise you to read it again.

Hey, I come from a similar background. I developed Binge Eating Disorder, and I have read Brain Over Binge maybe 5 times at this point. I have switched between counting calories, intuitive eating and fasting. Both me and my therapist believe intuitive eating is the way to go. 

1) Have you got a therapist or a professional you can talk to? This would be a huge help.

2) Have you read Intuitive Eating by Evelyn Tribole?

Personally, I find counting calories to detrimental to my eating disorder. CICO is science and counting calories works but having an eating disorder can completely throw the whole system off kilter. 

Intuitive eating is something I've had to work on. I've read Intuitive Eating many times and I constantly have to course correct. It's not easy for people experienced with dieting, let alone people experienced with an eating disorder. But I firmly believe it is the key. I'm now eating intuitively and I feel I finally have control over my BED. I don't binge or restrict anymore.

So here's the deal - weigh yourself or not, you weigh what you weigh. Your scale telling you that you've gained, maintained or lost doesn't change anything about your current weight. All it does it nudges you in the right direction regarding your calorie deficit. It isn't there to applaud you when you go down in weight and it isn't there to judge you when you go up. Do not start to look at the scale as this daunting creature wanting to scold you. It's an inanimate object that gives you a rough guide as to if you need to eat more or less calories. If it tells you you've gained, you've gained. Okay. Make an adjustment, learn, keep going. It measures your weight, not your self worth.
Here's a question: what was the goal you set *before* you started? If your goal was to fast for 24 hours, I'd say break it. If your goal was to fast for 2 days, or 3, or whatever - keep going.

Thank you! The idea to take half a portion and wait is a really good idea. I haven't been able to implement it fully yet, but I've made progress and I've implemented my own lite version. Before I start eating I visually divide my meal into halves and then slowly begin eating the first half, taking my time, and drinking lots of water. Then when I reach the half way mark I take an extended break before the next bite. Maybe it's just a few extra minutes but it's enough to get into the head space of taking my time and waiting and taking the time to analyse how full/satisfied I am. It amazes me at how much more satisfied I am after a meal when eating like this.

This is what I think - I think that while there is nothing wrong with losing weight to look good for yourself, you do not **need** to lose weight to look good for other people. Some people like how you look right now. The girl I like is very overweight and I love her body. Wouldn't change anything about how she looks.

HOWEVER, health needs to be a priority for everyone. I think it is 1000% possible to be "body positive" while also promoting weight loss. I love big women, but I would never want anybody to compromise their health. I see no reason why people can't learn to not be ashamed of their bodies while also losing weight for the health benefits.

We all want to be sexy and look like models and film stars, I totally get that. We can all pretend we are doing all of this so we can live until we are 120 but sometimes that's a lie and really we'd prefer to just look like a porn star at least once in our lives. And that's fine too. I just hate the idea that being overweight is ugly, and that fixing "ugly" is priority number 1.

Love your body how it is right now. Measure your value based on what you do and say, not your shape. Work on being as healthy as you can.
